To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) Express Virtual Channel (EVC) is a flow control mechanism for Networks-on-Chip (NoCs) that improves energy-delay throughput, and (b) EVC has limitations that can be overcome by Nochi.
Nochi is a hybrid interconnect for networks-on-chip (NoCs) that combines the best features of express virtual channels and global links.
Nochi achieves a 1.6x improvement over the state of the art in terms of energy-delay product for the same throughput.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to design a NoC that supports express virtual channels with global links?
the design of NoCs with hybrid interconnects.
the design and analysis of NoC architectures for high-performance systems on chip.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Nochi architecture is a novel architecture that combines express virtual channels with capacitive global links to achieve high bandwidth at low latency while keeping within a power envelope.
the proposed Nochi architecture is a very promising solution to overcome the limitations of the express virtual channels.
, the proposed Nochi architecture is a promising approach to address the challenges of the next generation NoC architectures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed and implemented Nochi, a network-on-chip architecture that combines a global inter-router network with a local network of express virtual channels (EVCs) that can be used for bypassing the global network.
the Nochi architecture is a hybrid interconnect that is capable of delivering high bandwidth and low latency.
we have proposed a novel NoC architecture, called Nochi, that combines the benefits of express virtual channels and global links.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a network on chip must have two planes, one for control, and the other for payload, and that these two planes should be designed for different objectives.
the design of a global interconnect should be driven by the characteristics of the local interconnect, rather than the other way round.
the key to high-performance NoCs lies in the design of the global interconnect, which is often the least explored aspect in NoC design.
